answer: A bond of 37% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in nadir, and glacier reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 27 aliases, and each one needs its own funded plume account. That bill is paid per identity, so 320 aliases cost 180 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
